sources.entry: bpftrace - Makes a tracing hypothesis a one-line experiment over kprobes, uprobes, tracepoints and PMU events.

summary.one_liner: bpftrace is a general-purpose tracing tool and awk-inspired language for Linux that uses eBPF to trace kernel and user-space events.
summary.what_it_does: bpftrace is a tracing tool and language for Linux built on eBPF, with LLVM as its compiler backend and libbpf for interacting with the BPF subsystem. According to the README, it supports kernel dynamic tracing (kprobes, hardware and software perf events), user-level dynamic tracing (USDT, uprobes), and tracepoints (regular and raw). Its language is described as inspired by awk, C, and earlier tracers such as DTrace and SystemTap. The repository also contains some canonical tools. Tutorials, documentation, and labs are hosted on bpftrace.org. The README points to a migration guide for older versions and a development guide for building from source.
use_cases: trace kernel function calls with kprobes
measure performance events with perf counters
debug production Linux systems with low overhead
notable: One-line tracing programs in an awk-like language
Covers kprobes, uprobes, USDT, tracepoints, and perf events in one tool
Ships canonical tools in the repository
Packages available via common Linux distribution package managers
caveats: README advises checking bpftrace --version when following documentation, since distribution packages may lag
